faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a dental prosthetist in Australia?
faqs.a: Dental prosthetist rates vary by award classification and experience. Under the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020, minimum rates are set by the Fair Work Commission. For award-free employees, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Many dental prosthetists earn above the minimum, and you can check the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides for the relevant award.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on a dental prosthetist salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026) up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on an annual salary of $79,040, super would be an additional $9,484.80, bringing total remuneration to $88,524.80.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on a dental prosthetist salary of $80,000?
faqs.a: Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates, on $80,000 you pay nil on the first $18,200, then 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020), and 30% on the remaining $35,000 ($10,500). Total tax is $14,520, plus the Medicare levy of 2% ($1,600), giving a total of $16,120. Your take-home pay would be approximately $63,880 per year, or $1,228 per week.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Dental Prosthetist Salary

If you're a dental prosthetist in Australia, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential for budgeting and tax planning. This guide uses the latest figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission to help you convert your **dental prosthetist salary** accurately.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The standard formula to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a full‑time week of 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the National Employment Standards. For example, if your hourly rate is $40.00:

- Annual: $40 × 38 × 52 = **$79,040**
- Weekly: $79,040 ÷ 52 = **$1,520**
- Fortnightly: $1,520 × 2 = **$3,040**

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more personalised estimate, use [the timesheet](/) on our site.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

Most dental prosthetists are covered by the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020** (or a similar award). The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database contains the minimum rates for each classification. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75% following the Annual Wage Review. You can find the exact rate for your classification in the [pay guides](/blog) published by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

If you are award‑free (not covered by any award or agreement), the **National Minimum Wage** applies:
- $26.44 per hour
- $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this works.

### Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Dental Prosthetist Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|----------------|-------------------|
| $0 – $18,200 | Nil |
| $18,201 – $45,000 | 15¢ for each $1 over $18,200 |
| $45,001 – $135,000 | $4,020 plus 30¢ for each $1 over $45,000 |
| $135,001 – $190,000 | $31,020 plus 37¢ for each $1 over $135,000 |
| $190,001+ | $51,370 plus 45¢ for each $1 over $190,000 |

In addition, the **Medicare levy** is generally 2% of your taxable income (with reductions for low income earners). For the 2025–26 year, the single reduction threshold is used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in our reference. The levy is applied after the tax-free threshold.

**Example for a dental prosthetist earning $79,040:**
- Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($79,040 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $10,212 = **$14,232**
- Medicare levy: 2% × $79,040 = **$1,580.80**
- Total tax and levy: **$15,812.80**
- Net annual pay: **$63,227.20**
- Net weekly: **$1,215.91**

For a detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of **12%** of your ordinary time earnings (from 1 July 2026), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is paid **on top** of your salary, not deducted from it.

For a dental prosthetist salary of $79,040:
- Super: 12% × $79,040 = **$9,484.80**
- Total remuneration: $79,040 + $9,484.80 = **$88,524.80**

If your salary exceeds the maximum contribution base, super is capped. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Using the example above:
- Fortnightly gross: $3,040
- Fortnightly net (after tax and Medicare): approximately $2,431.82

This can help you plan your budget and compare job offers. Our [reference tables](/data) provide quick conversion charts for common hourly rates.

### Important Disclaimer

The figures here are estimates. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming consistent hours and no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For the most accurate information, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides and the Fair Work Commission National Minimum Wage page.

### Using Our Timesheet

To calculate your own **dental prosthetist salary**, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate. If you work casually, check the box to add 25% casual loading. The tool will show your annual, weekly, and fortnightly figures, along with estimated tax and super. Remember to enter your base rate **before** casual loading – the tool adds it automatically.

For more on hourly conversion, see our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide. If you're comparing job offers, our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page has tips on evaluating total remuneration.

### Summary

Converting your dental prosthetist salary from hourly to annual is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks. Then subtract tax and Medicare levy, and add super on top. Always check your specific award or agreement for the correct minimum rate. Use our tools and the official Fair Work resources to stay informed.
